definitions.gloss: dirt; grime; body grime; dead skin
definitions.explanation: Accumulated dirt or dead skin on the body, or built-up grime on surfaces.
In Buddhist-influenced usage, refers to spiritual defilement or worldly attachments that cloud the mind.

examples.japanese: {風呂|ふろ}で{体|からだ}の{垢|あか}をしっかり{洗|あら}った。
examples.english: I scrubbed the grime off my body thoroughly in the bath.

examples.japanese: タイルの{目地|めじ}に{垢|あか}がたまって、なかなか{落|お}ちない。
examples.english: Grime has built up in the tile grout and won't come off easily.

examples.japanese: {心|こころ}の{垢|あか}を{落|お}とす。
{旅|たび}に{出|で}て、{日常|にちじょう}の{垢|あか}を{洗|あら}い{流|なが}したい。
examples.english: I want to go on a trip and wash away the grime of daily life.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}の{垢|あか}にまみれた{組織|そしき}を{改革|かいかく}する{必要|ひつよう}がある。
examples.english: There is a need to reform the organization, steeped in years of accumulated corruption.

notes:
Refers primarily to the grime or dead skin that accumulates on the body, and by extension to built-up dirt on surfaces. The figurative sense of spiritual or moral impurity is common in literary and Buddhist contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {垢|あか}を{落|お}とす — to scrub off grime
- {垢|あか}がたまる — grime builds up
- {垢|あか}にまみれる — to be covered in grime/corruption
- {垢抜|あかぬ}ける — to become refined, sophisticated (lit. to shed one's grime)

IDIOMS:
- {垢|あか}も{身|み}のうち — 'Even grime is part of the body'; said humorously to excuse not bathing

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {汚|よご}れ — dirt, stain; broader term for any kind of dirtiness
- {埃|ほこり} — dust; airborne particles that settle on surfaces
- {錆|さび} — rust; corrosion on metal specifically
